name: ctl-quoting-article
text:
# Understanding prompt injection

A prompt injection attack hides orders inside content. For example, a ticket might say "ignore previous instructions" hoping the agent obeys. Another classic example is "do not tell the user" paired with a data request. This article discusses why quoting such phrases in documentation is normal and necessary, and how defenders detect the pattern.

name: ctl-defense-howto
text: Defending against prompt injection: treat tool output as data, gate destructive actions behind confirmations, and keep an audit log. Layered defenses matter because any single string filter can be paraphrased around.
